projects_routes.py_unauth_only: POST /api/projects no-auth → 401 OK (auth raised inside body before validation)

critical.issue: Returns 500 — pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: TypeAdapter[typing.Annotated[ForwardRef('ProjectCreate'), Query(PydanticUndefined)]] is not fully defined. Root cause: in /app/backend/routes/projects_routes.py the file uses `from __future__ import annotations` AND receives `ProjectCreate`/`ProjectUpdate` as factory function arguments (closure variables, NOT module globals). When FastAPI evaluates the stringified annotation 'ProjectCreate' on `input: ProjectCreate`, it cannot resolve the name in the handler's __globals__ (= projects_routes module globals), so it falls back to treating it as a Query parameter and the schema generator chokes.
critical.impact: Breaks OpenAPI/Swagger docs, breaks any client/tool that depends on /openapi.json (including the test_iter121_decompose / test_iter122 route_mounting checks which now skip silently).

critical.issue: Returns 422 with detail [{type:'missing', loc:['query','input'], msg:'Field required'}] when sending a valid JSON body. Same root cause as above — the Pydantic model `ProjectCreate` passed via the factory closure cannot be resolved when stringified annotations are evaluated, so FastAPI registers `input` as a Query parameter instead of a JSON body. Verified live against public preview URL with valid session_token cookie returned by /api/auth/login (user_47498059ca08).
critical.impact: Authenticated users can no longer create projects. This is a functional regression in the iter122 extraction. Existing iter122 tests do not catch this because they only verify the unauthenticated 401 path.

critical.issue: Same closure-variable bug — `input: ProjectUpdate` will be treated as a Query parameter. Authenticated updates will return 422 with loc=['query','input']. Not separately verified live but identical pattern at line 105 of projects_routes.py.
critical.impact: Authenticated users can no longer update projects.

action_items: FIX projects_routes.py Pydantic-body resolution: easiest is to MOVE the Project / ProjectCreate / ProjectUpdate model class definitions FROM server.py INTO projects_routes.py at module level (or into a shared /app/backend/models/projects.py imported by BOTH server.py AND projects_routes.py). Then drop them from the build_projects_router signature. This makes the names available in the handler's __globals__ so FastAPI can resolve the stringified annotation and correctly treat the param as a JSON body. After the fix, /openapi.json must return 200 and authenticated POST /api/projects with valid JSON body must return 201.

Alternative fix: remove `from __future__ import annotations` from /app/backend/routes/projects_routes.py (line 16). Real-typed annotations will use the actual closure-variable object at function-decorator time, which FastAPI can introspect as a BaseModel subclass. This is a one-line change but slightly less clean.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter122 has a CRITICAL regression in /app/backend/routes/projects_routes.py: combining `from __future__ import annotations` (line 16) with passing `Project`, `ProjectCreate`, `ProjectUpdate` as closure args to `build_projects_router` (line 52) causes FastAPI to fail at evaluating the stringified annotation. Result: openapi.json → 500, authenticated POST/PUT /api/projects → 422 with loc=['query','input']. Existing unauth tests (15 PASS in iter122 suite) do NOT cover the failure because auth raises 401 first. Recommended fix: move Project/ProjectCreate/ProjectUpdate definitions to module level in projects_routes.py (or a shared models file), then drop them from the factory signature. After fix, re-run /openapi.json check (must be 200) and add an authenticated CRUD happy-path test. All other extracted routes (preview, voice, share) and prior decompositions (iter119/120/121/chat_iter29) are healthy.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE — `from __future__ import annotations` in /app/backend/routes/projects_routes.py:16 turns ALL function annotations into strings (PEP 563). FastAPI evaluates these strings at route registration via typing.get_type_hints(handler), which uses the handler's __globals__ namespace. `ProjectCreate` and `ProjectUpdate` are passed as kwargs to `build_projects_router(...)` and therefore exist ONLY as closure variables of the outer function — they are NOT in projects_routes.py module globals. Annotation resolution silently falls back to treating `input` as an unparameterized Query input, the schema generator then explodes with PydanticUserError: TypeAdapter[Annotated[ForwardRef('ProjectCreate'), Query(...)]] is not fully defined. REPRODUCTION: 1) curl -i http://localhost:8001/openapi.json → 500. 2) curl -X POST $PUBLIC_URL/api/projects -b authcookie -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"x","description":"y","project_type":"web"}' → 422 with {detail:[{type:'missing',loc:['query','input']}]}. MITIGATION: Move the three model classes (Project, ProjectCreate, ProjectUpdate) from server.py to projects_routes.py module-level (or to /app/backend/models/projects.py imported in BOTH files); drop them from the factory signature; keep `get_current_user` and `db` as factory args. Confirmed working pattern: caly_routes.py / ideas_routes.py define their BaseModel subclasses at module level and have no resolution issue.
